items.t: Recognize Reverend David Meredith for his service and advocacy for LGBTQ inclusion
items.sm: Recognizes Reverend David Meredith for his contributions to the United Methodist Church, his work for marginalized people and his advocacy for full inclusion of LGBTQ persons since 1984.

items.t: Establish "William J. Loftin Way" as an honorary name for Clay Street
items.sm: Establishes the honorary secondary name "William J. Loftin Way" for Clay Street between East 14th Street and Melindy Street, honoring Cincinnati Police Department officer William Jefferson Loftin.

FYI MEMO, submitted by Councilmember Mann, from Patrick A. Duhaney, Acting City
Establish "William J. Loftin Way" as an honorary name for Clay Street
items.sm: Establishes the honorary secondary name "William J. Loftin Way" for Clay Street between East 14th Street and Melindy Street, honoring Cincinnati Police Department officer William Jefferson Loftin.

items.t: Establish accessible public vehicle regulations in Chapter 407 of the Municipal Code
items.sm: Modifies Chapter 407, "Public Vehicles," of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to set minimum standards for public vehicles accessible to passengers with disabilities and repeal the handicapped livery vehicle provisions.

items.t: Request a report on a property tax cap program for low-income seniors
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on the feasibility and merit of a program capping property taxes for low-income seniors, like the one in Philadelphia.

items.t: Resolution on public safety criteria for siting natural gas pipelines in Ohio
items.sm: Recognizes the need for Ohio to add public safety criteria, setbacks and zoning requirements to natural gas pipeline siting and encourages the Ohio General Assembly to enact such legislation.

items.t: Ask the Administration to work with Cincinnati Public Schools on pedestrian safety
items.sm: Asks the City Administration to work with Cincinnati Public Schools to prioritize pedestrian safety hot spots near schools, report back in 90 days and use part of the $500,000 allocation for them.

items.t: Amend the Rules of Council on meetings, appointments, referrals and committees
items.sm: Asks Council to amend Rules 1.7, 3.5, 7.9, 10.2 and 10.8 covering staff meetings, mayoral appointments, Council referrals, standing committees and committee reports.

Ask the City Manager to end the State Lobbying contract and fund addiction treatment
items.sm: Asks the City Manager to end the $8,000 per month State Lobbying contract and direct the unencumbered $88,000 for fiscal year 2019 to the Center for Addiction Treatment.

items.t: Ask to increase the Riverfront Park fund by $500,000 and fund Cintrifuse and CincyTech
items.sm: Asks Council to increase the Fund 329 Riverfront Park appropriation by $500,000, freeing General Fund money to give $300,000 to Cintrifuse and $200,000 to CincyTech.

items.t: Ask to allocate minority chamber of commerce funding by population share
items.sm: Asks that City Budget funds for the four Greater Cincinnati minority chambers of commerce be allocated proportionally by each chamber's share of the Greater Cincinnati MSA population under the latest census data.

Ask to amend the budget ordinances to reallocate funds to several programs
items.sm: Asks Council to amend the budget ordinances to give $500,000 each to CincyTech and Cintrifuse combined and to the East Price Hill Masonic Fund, plus $225,000 to three other programs.

items.t: Enact a 5 percent Parking Occupancy Tax on parking lots and garages
items.sm: Enacts Chapter 310 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code, imposing a 5 percent tax on the fee charged for parking motor vehicles in City parking lots and garages.

items.t: Ask to reallocate $183,000 of the fiscal year 2018 fund balance to CincyTech and Cintrifuse
items.sm: Asks Council to reallocate $183,000 of the fiscal year 2018 fund balance to the fiscal year 2019 General Fund as equal leveraged support for CincyTech and Cintrifuse.

items.t: Increase commercial waste franchise fees and authorize fiscal year 2019 budget transfers
items.sm: Increases commercial waste franchise fees effective July 1, 2018, authorizes General Fund and capital transfers funding Council's budget changes, and repeals the vehicle immobilization sections of Ordinance No. 0152-2018.

items.t: Presentation on the Sidney Road zone change from SF-4 to CC-M
items.sm: Presents the proposed zone change for Sidney Road from SF-4 to CC-M, submitted by the Acting City Manager.

items.t: Rezone 2446 Kipling Avenue in Mt. Airy to a single-family district
items.sm: Amends the official zoning map to rezone 2446 Kipling Avenue in Mt. Airy from the IR Institutional Residential district to the SF-6 Single-Family district.

items.t: Presentation on the Ronald McDonald House (PD-52) expansion
items.sm: Presents information from the Acting City Manager on the expansion of the Ronald McDonald House (PD-52).

items.t: Presentation on the zone change at 3110-3126 Woodburn Avenue in Evanston
items.sm: Presents the City Planning Department's slideshow on changing the zoning of 3110-3126 Woodburn Avenue, Merrimac Square in Evanston, from CN-P to RM-0.7.

items.t: Presentation on rezoning 2446 Kipling Avenue from IR to SF-6
items.sm: Presents a proposal from the Acting City Manager to rezone 2446 Kipling Avenue from Industrial Regional (IR) to Single-Family (SF-6).

items.t: Approve a $4,422,596 fiscal year 2019 budget for the Cincinnati Bell Connector
items.sm: Approves a $4,422,596 operations and maintenance budget for the Cincinnati Bell Connector and appropriates $2,985,458 from Fund 455, Streetcar Operations, for fiscal year 2019 streetcar requirements.

items.t: Authorize a property sale agreement with Benton Block, LLC in Over-the-Rhine
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute an agreement selling City property at 1712-18 Vine Street and 1659-63 Hamer Street near Grant Park to Benton Block, LLC.

items.t: Authorize an encroachment easement for stairs at 19-27 West Clifton Avenue
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to grant Morgan Apartments LLC an encroachment easement over West Clifton Avenue right-of-way for the construction, use, maintenance and repair of stairs in Over-the-Rhine.

items.t: Accept a $212,369 state grant for the Ohio River Trail West extension
items.sm: Establishes a capital project account and authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate up to $212,369 from the Ohio Department of Natural Resources Clean Ohio Trails Fund for a trail extension in Riverside.

items.t: Authorize land exchange with school district for Hirsch Recreation Center expansion
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to convey a parcel at 3638 Reading Road in Avondale to the Cincinnati City School District in exchange for a similar parcel.

items.t: Authorize a ground lease with BLOC Ministries, Inc. for a horse riding academy
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to lease approximately 7 acres at 1655 Ross Avenue in East Price Hill to BLOC Ministries, Inc. for a horse riding academy for up to 30 years.

items.t: Authorize a $7,324,742 SAFER grant for 40 Fire Department recruits
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $7,324,742 from the fiscal year 2017 SAFER grant to partially fund 40 Cincinnati Fire Department recruits for three years.

items.t: Report on compliance with Section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act
items.sm: Presents a report from the City Manager on the City's compliance with Section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

items.t: Approve an 11-year tax exemption agreement with Race and Vine Offices LLC
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Race and Vine Offices LLC for remodeling buildings at 1502 Vine Street, 1434 Vine Street and 1537 Race Street.

items.t: Accept state property along I-71 and amend the purchase option agreement
items.sm: Accepts property from the Ohio Department of Transportation near Martin Luther King Jr. Drive and Reading Road and authorizes an amended purchase option agreement with Uptown SEQ Holdings, LLC.

items.t: Authorize a tax exemption agreement with Cincinnati Brewery District Apartments LLC
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Cincinnati Brewery District Apartments LLC for a 12-year, 100% exemption at 1906 Elm Street in Over-the-Rhine.

items.t: Levy special assessments for the 2145 Dana Avenue energy project
items.sm: Levies special assessments for the assessment project at 2145 Dana Avenue involving the City of Cincinnati, Ohio Energy Special Improvement District.

items.t: Vacate the pedestrian and vehicular easement over former St. James Alley
items.sm: Vacates a permanent easement for pedestrian and vehicular traffic over the former St. James Alley between E. McMillan Street and Curtis Street in Walnut Hills.

items.t: Authorize transfers and appropriations of $8,575,300 for capital improvement projects
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $8,575,300 from enterprise and restricted funds to Fund 980 capital projects, appropriating water works, lead service line and stormwater funds, and accepting Metropolitan Sewer District resources.

items.t: Repeal Ordinance No. 134-2018 on a Madisonville property tax exemption
items.sm: Repeals Ordinance No. 134-2018, which granted a real property tax exemption for improvements in Madisonville to be built under an agreement with Ackermann Enterprises, Inc.

items.t: Authorize $11,065,000 in bonds for street improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue bonds or notes in anticipation of bonds in the principal amount of $11,065,000 for street improvements.

items.t: Authorize $1,950,000 in bonds for parks and recreation improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue bonds or notes in anticipation of bonds in the principal amount of $1,950,000 for parks and recreation improvements.

items.t: Authorize $10,930,000 in bonds for public building improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue bonds or notes in anticipation of bonds in the principal amount of $10,930,000 for public building improvements.

items.t: Authorize interim financing for the Capital Acceleration Plan
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager or the Fiscal Officer to enter into a bond anticipation note line of credit or fixed rate notes to fund the Capital Acceleration Plan.

items.t: Authorize up to $100,000,000 in bonds to refund general obligation bonds
items.sm: Authorizes the issuance and sale of bonds of up to $100,000,000 to refund outstanding City general obligation bonds and sets a refunding savings threshold.

items.t: Authorize up to $2,500,000 in revenue bonds for industrial site redevelopment
items.sm: Authorizes the issuance of up to $2,500,000 in Economic Development Revenue Bonds, or notes, for the Industrial Site Redevelopment Project, with a pledge of certain revenues.

items.t: Authorize up to $750,000 in bonds for East Price Hill revitalization improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the issuance, sale and delivery of up to $750,000 in Economic Development Revenue Bonds, or notes in anticipation of them, to finance East Price Hill Revitalization Permanent Improvements.

items.t: Declare Walnut Hills improvements a public purpose with a 30-year tax exemption
items.sm: Declares improvements at 743-769 E. McMillan Street, 2438 and 2420 Concord Street and 718-752 Wayne Street a public purpose, exempt from real property taxation for 30 years.

items.t: Establish the priority order of property tax exemptions in the Walnut Hills Incentive District
items.sm: Establishes the priority order of property tax exemptions for parcels on E. McMillan, Concord and Wayne Streets for a 739 E McMillan St, LLC development.

items.t: Authorize a $1,000,000 federal grant for the PIVOT Initiative and victim services
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate a $1,000,000 U.S. Department of Justice grant to expand the PIVOT Initiative and victim and witness services.

items.t: Approve a Job Creation Tax Credit Agreement with The Kroger Co. for 590 jobs
items.sm: Authorizes a Job Creation Tax Credit Agreement with The Kroger Co. for 590 new jobs at 221 East Fourth Street, with a 40% City income tax credit for 5 years.

items.t: Increase commercial waste franchise fees and appropriate $2,000,000
items.sm: Amends Section 730-17 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to increase commercial waste franchise fees effective July 1, 2018, and appropriates $2,000,000 for the City's recycling program, an Environmental Programs Manager and economic development programs.

items.t: Authorize fee increases to generate $3,811,600 for fiscal year 2019 programs
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to raise procurement, pre-development, Office of Administrative Hearings and parking fees to generate $3,811,600 for economic development programs and the Cincinnati Health Department's needle exchange program.

items.t: Increase the monthly stormwater charge to $4.64 and appropriate $3,400,000
items.sm: Amends Ordinance No. 68-2018 to raise the stormwater charge to $4.64 per equivalent runoff unit on August 1, 2018, and appropriates $3,400,000 for trash pickup and flood control.

items.t: Approve a $4,472,596 fiscal year 2019 budget for the Cincinnati Bell Connector
items.sm: Approves a $4,472,596 operations and maintenance budget for the Cincinnati Bell Connector and appropriates $3,035,458 from Fund 455, "Streetcar Operations," including funding to hire a new streetcar executive.

items.t: Authorize an application for a $25,000,000 BUILD grant for the Western Hills Viaduct
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for up to $25,000,000 from the United States Department of Transportation BUILD program for demolition and construction of portions of a new Western Hills Viaduct.

items.t: Authorize FEMA reimbursement for February 2018 flood costs and establish Fund 479
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for and accept Federal Emergency Management Agency reimbursement for February 2018 flood response costs and establishes Fund 479, "FEMA -2018 Flood."

items.t: Transfer $1,040,000 among capital funds for the fiscal year 2019 capital budget
items.sm: Authorizes the transfer and return to source of $1,040,000 from Funds 758, 858 and 870, and reappropriates it to capital improvement project accounts for the fiscal year 2019 General Capital Budget.

items.t: Levy an excise tax on outdoor advertising signs
items.sm: Establishes an Outdoor Advertising Sign Excise Tax on the privilege of installing, placing and maintaining outdoor advertising signs in the City, by adding Chapter 313 and Section 895-27 and amending Section 1501-8.

items.t: Levy special assessments for street lighting in Lighting Group 1
items.sm: Levies special assessments to pay a portion of the cost of special street lighting in Lighting Group 1 for the three-year period beginning on August 1, 2017.

items.t: Declare the necessity of the 2145 Dana Avenue assessment project
items.sm: Declares by legislative resolution the necessity of the assessment project at 2145 Dana Avenue involving the City of Cincinnati, Ohio Energy Special Improvement District.

items.t: Establish the St. Clair Recreation Area Improvements project and accept $320,000
items.sm: Establishes a capital project account and accepts and appropriates $320,000 from the Metropolitan Sewer District for athletic field renovations, parking lot improvements and ADA access at the St. Clair Recreation Area.

items.t: Establish a grant process for wheelchair accessible taxicab conversions
items.sm: Establishes a process for grants from the "Wheelchair Accessible Taxicabs" project account to help taxicab owners convert vehicles to meet the updated standards in Cincinnati Municipal Code Chapter 407, "Public Vehicles."

items.t: Authorize a Property Sale and Development Agreement for 111 and 113 W. Elder Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute an agreement with 111-13 W. Elder St. LLC to sell the upper levels of the City-owned buildings at 111 and 113 W. Elder Street for residential redevelopment.

items.t: Establish the Pride Crosswalk project account and accept an $8,000 donation
items.sm: Establishes capital improvement project account no. 980x233x182324, "Pride Crosswalk," and authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate an $8,000 donation from the Cincinnati Center City Development Corporation.

items.t: Authorize a tax exemption agreement with Riverside Drive Enterprises LLC for River Road
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Riverside Drive Enterprises LLC for a 15-year, 100% exemption at 2746-2790 River Road in Sedamsville.

items.t: Authorize a tax exemption agreement with Findlaomi LLC for 1706 Central Parkway
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Findlaomi LLC for a 10-year, 80% exemption at 1706 Central Parkway in Over-the-Rhine.

items.t: Authorize the sale of the Shillito west building to Neyer Properties, Incorporated
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Property Sale and Development Agreement with Neyer Properties, Incorporated to sell 137 W. 7th Street for a mixed-use project with office, retail and parking.

items.t: Appropriate $445,031,730 for fiscal year 2019 restricted revenue funds
items.sm: Appropriates $445,031,730 from the City's restricted revenue funds for operating requirements, capital outlay and debt service for fiscal year 2019, and authorizes related transfers to the Bond Retirement Fund and garage reserve accounts.

items.t: Ask the Law Department to draft a Charter Amendment for a 2.0% Admissions Tax increase
items.sm: Asks the Law Department to draft an ordinance placing a Charter Amendment on the November 2018 ballot for a 2.0% Admissions Tax increase funding United Way administered Human Services and Neighborhoods.

items.t: Authorize a loan of up to $200,000 for a Findlay Market restaurant incubator
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Funding Agreement with the Corporation For Findlay Market of Cincinnati for a City loan up to $200,000 to build out a restaurant incubator at 1807-1809 Elm Street.

items.t: Authorize the sale of the upper levels of 118 W. Elder Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Property Sale and Development Agreement with Andrew Reider and Rachel Reider to sell the upper levels of the City-owned building at 118 W. Elder Street for residential redevelopment.

items.t: Authorize $7,540,000 in bonds for equipment improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue bonds or notes in anticipation of bonds in the principal amount of $7,540,000 for equipment improvements.

items.t: Authorize $17,381,500 in notes for street improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue notes in the principal amount of $17,381,500 in anticipation of bonds to fund street improvements.

items.t: Authorize $2,178,000 in notes for recreation improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue notes in the principal amount of $2,178,000 in anticipation of bonds to fund recreation improvements.

items.t: Authorize $2,077,000 in notes for park improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue notes in the principal amount of $2,077,000 in anticipation of bonds to fund park improvements.

items.t: Authorize $4,415,000 in bonds for stormwater improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City to issue bonds, or notes in anticipation of bonds, in the principal amount of $4,415,000 to make stormwater improvements.

items.t: Authorize a $250,000 transfer for Buildings and Inspections personnel needs
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $100,000 and $150,000 from two accounts to another account within the Department of Buildings and Inspections to realign funds for the Department's ongoing personnel needs.

items.t: Authorize transfers of $1,040,000 among capital funds for the fiscal year 2019 capital budget
items.sm: Authorizes returning $1,040,000 from capital project accounts to Funds 758, 858 and 870 and appropriating it to other capital projects in the fiscal year 2019 General Capital Budget.

items.t: Authorize enhanced building permit and property maintenance fees and appropriate $3,658,125
items.sm: Authorizes the Director of Buildings and Inspections to charge enhanced fees, amends the Cincinnati Municipal Code, and appropriates $3,658,125 to maintain permitting and property maintenance services.

items.t: Approve the fiscal year 2019 Capital Improvement Program and Budget
items.sm: Approves and adopts the fiscal year 2019 Capital Improvement Program and Budget, appropriates funds, authorizes related transfers, and establishes the new "Development ROW Improvements" project account.

items.t: Levy an excise tax on outdoor advertising signs in Cincinnati
items.sm: Creates an excise tax on the privilege of installing, placing and maintaining outdoor advertising signs in the City, and amends the related Municipal Code chapters and civil offenses section.

items.t: Revise water service rates for unincorporated Hamilton County effective September 1, 2018 (Version B)
items.sm: Amends Chapter 401 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to revise Greater Cincinnati Water Works rates for unincorporated Hamilton County areas effective September 1, 2018 (Version B).

items.t: Transfer $1,040,000 among capital funds for the fiscal year 2019 capital budget
items.sm: Authorizes the transfer and return to source of $1,040,000 from Funds 758, 858 and 870, and reappropriates it to capital improvement project accounts for the fiscal year 2019 General Capital Budget.

items.t: Transfer and appropriate $335,500 for police overtime and economic development
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $100,000 from the General Fund surplus and $235,500 from operating accounts to fund police overtime, economic development initiatives, the Greater Cincinnati Redevelopment Authority and the state Legislative Agent contract.

items.t: Override Mayor Cranley's veto of Document 201801158
items.sm: Asks Council to override Mayor Cranley's veto of Document 201801158, as moved verbally by Councilmembers Young and Landsman.

items.t: Honor Michael Chanak Jr. for his work for the LGBT community
items.sm: Recognizes and honors Michael Chanak Jr. for his work on behalf of the lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender community.

items.t: Reconsider Mayor Cranley's veto of Document 201801158
items.sm: Asks Council to reconsider Mayor Cranley's veto of Document 201801158, as moved verbally by Councilmembers Young and Landsman.

items.t: COMMUNICATION, submitted by Councilmember Seelbach from Akshay Ahuja, regarding Yard Citation.

Urge the federal government to reverse harmful immigration policies
items.sm: Urges the President and the United States Congress to reverse the current administration's immigration policies and ensure policy reflects American values on human rights and dignity, especially for children.

items.t: Recognize Father Benjamin J. Urmston for 47 years at Xavier University
items.sm: Recognizes Father Benjamin J. Urmston for his lifelong contributions to the Catholic Church, 47 years of service at Xavier University and advocacy for peace and social justice.

items.t: Evaluate City management of the Cincinnati Bell Connector instead of SORTA
items.sm: Asks the Administration to evaluate removing the Southwest Ohio Regional Transit Authority as streetcar operator and establishing direct City management, and to answer six questions on costs, federal role, legal issues and timeline.

items.t: Rezone 5016 Sidney Road in West Price Hill to a commercial district
items.sm: Amends the official zoning map to rezone 5016 Sidney Road in West Price Hill from the SF-4 Single-Family Residential district to the CC-M Commercial Community-Mixed district.

items.t: Request engagement on "The Dream Campus" development with two Reading Road churches
items.sm: Asks the Administration to engage New Friendship Baptist Church and Temple Bible College on "The Dream Campus," pause code citations, review zoning and report back with development recommendations.

items.t: Report on vacant buildings in the City of Cincinnati
items.sm: Reports on vacant buildings in the City, submitted by Acting City Manager Patrick A. Duhaney in response to an adopted motion, Document #201800515.

items.t: Rezone 2.026 acres at 3110-3126 Woodburn Avenue in Evanston
items.sm: Amends the official zoning map to rezone 2.026 acres at 3110-3126 Woodburn Avenue in Evanston from Commercial Neighborhood-Pedestrian (CN-P) to Residential Multi-Family (RM-0.7).

items.t: Define "worker" for the pre-apprenticeship training fund in water and sewer construction contracts
items.sm: Ordains new Section 320-1-W of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to define "worker" for purposes of the pre-apprenticeship training fund in Section 320-7.

items.t: Approve a major amendment to Planned Development District No. 52
items.sm: Approves a major amendment to the concept plan and development program statement for Planned Development District No. 52 to build a new building with additional guest rooms and parking.

items.t: Define "worker" for the pre-apprenticeship training fund in water and sewer construction contracts
items.sm: Ordains new Section 320-1-W of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to define "worker" for purposes of the pre-apprenticeship training fund in Section 320-7 (Version B).

items.t: Request a report and action plan from the Administration on tree removal
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on trees marked for removal and on the preventative maintenance list, and to present an action plan with costs for removing and managing at-risk trees.

items.t: Ordain new Chapter 870, "Land Installment Contracts," of the Municipal Code
items.sm: Ordains new Chapter 870, "Land Installment Contracts," to protect residents' rights and bring properties under land installment contracts into code compliance to prevent blight (Version B).

items.t: Request a report on outcomes of trash set-out citations
items.sm: Asks the Administration to prepare a report on the outcomes of all citations issued for late, early or improper trash set out since the Private Lot Abatement Program passed on March 25, 2105.

items.t: Transfer and appropriate $335,500 for police overtime and economic development
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $100,000 from the General Fund surplus and $235,500 from operating accounts to fund police overtime, regional economic development, chambers of commerce, CincyTech and Cintrifuse.

items.sm: Asks the City Administration to immediately suspend the 72-hour notice of evacuation given to residents of the Third Street encampments.

Communication on a request for bike lanes on Salem Road
items.sm: Transmits a communication from the Mt. Washington Community Council relaying a resident's request for bike lanes on Salem Road, now being repaved from Kellogg Ave to Wayside Ave.

items.t: Presentation on the Wage Implementation Project from the Cincinnati Union Co-op Initiative
items.sm: Presents the Wage Implementation Project from the Cincinnati Union Co-op Initiative, submitted by Councilmember Landsman.

items.sm: Submits to voters a measure lowering the earned income tax from 2% to 1.7% and adding a 0.1% tax for streets, parks, human services, economic development and community councils, if the transit sales tax passes.

items.sm: Submits to voters a Charter amendment creating an incentive for Cincinnati Public Schools Public Safety Academy graduates to pursue Fire Department careers (Version B).

items.t: Petition for the organization of the Banks Community Authority
items.sm: Submits a petition from the City Solicitor for the organization of the Banks Community Authority.

items.t: Authorize a grant of up to $101,932 from the FEMA Port Security Grant Program
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $101,932 to maintain Ohio River surveillance cameras and buy Zodiac boats and tracking equipment.

items.t: Authorize the transfer of $160,000 for golf course tree maintenance and mold remediation
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $160,000 from the Municipal Golf Activities Fund 105 surplus to the Recreation Department for tree maintenance, preventative landscaping and mold remediation at City golf courses.

items.t: Vacate public rights-of-way for the relocation of Stargel Stadium
items.sm: Vacates Hopkins, Weser, Essen, Danube and Munchen rights-of-way, dedicated but never accepted, south of Ezzard Charles Drive in the West End, for the relocation of Stargel Stadium.

items.t: Approve a 15-year tax exemption agreement with Paramount Square II, LLC
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Paramount Square II, LLC for a 100% exemption for remodeling five historic buildings in Walnut Hills.

items.t: Authorize a collective bargaining agreement with the Greater Cincinnati Building and Construction Trades Council
items.sm: Authorizes implementing the labor management agreement with the Greater Cincinnati Building and Construction Trades Council, AFL-CIO, and the City Manager to execute a new collective bargaining agreement.

items.t: Authorize an easement for an underground electrical vault on Walnut Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Grant of Easement for an underground electrical vault in the Walnut Street right-of-way serving a mixed-use development at Court Street and Walnut Street.

items.t: Authorize a Donation Agreement for the property at 6006 Belmont Ave
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Donation Agreement with the Hamilton County Land Reutilization Corporation for the property at 6006 Belmont Ave in College Hill.

items.t: Authorize applications for road and bridge construction grants and loans
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for Hamilton County Municipal Road Fund and Ohio Public Works Commission grants and loans, Round 33, for road and bridge projects throughout the City.

items.t: Authorize a grant of up to $12,000 for boating safety education
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $12,000 from the Ohio Department of Natural Resources for Cincinnati Recreation Commission boating safety programs, and deposit it in Fund 324.

items.t: Authorize $1,732,050 in grants for Westwood Avenue and Columbia Parkway improvements
items.sm: Establishes two capital project accounts and authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate grants totaling $1,732,050 for street, wall and bridge rehabilitation, including Westwood Avenue safety and the Columbia Parkway pier wall.

items.t: Establish a bridge maintenance fund and accept up to $5,000,000 from Hamilton County
